integrated_answer.claim: Account-nested routes expose index/create/update/destroy, without show. Index directly renders the account relation as a bare JSON array; create/update return the saved object; destroy returns head :ok. Creation uses Current.account.canned_responses.new; update/destroy find through that association. Strong parameters permit short_code/content. The model requires content, short_code and account, with short_code unique per account.

Search removes NUL bytes, uses a bound case-insensitive substring predicate against short_code OR content, then orders prefix short_code matches (1), other short_code matches (0.5), and content matches (0.2) descending. Ranking fragments use sanitize_sql_array. SQL quoting/binding does not mean literal wildcard escaping: the inspected code does not explicitly escape percent/underscore. Without search it returns Current.account.canned_responses.

The server array and client cache contract align. CannedResponse overrides extraction to response.data and marshalling to {data:rows}, replacing the generic payload hooks; cache hits and network reads therefore present rows at response.data. refetchAndCommit invokes extraction and returns the original network response; valid nonempty cache hits invoke marshalling. No shape defect follows from generic defaults. get(false), the default, uses network; invalid/empty cached rows refetch, while initial IndexedDB initialization failure falls back to network.

The accountScoped singleton resolves URL account IDs from window.location.pathname at read time. The cache dataManager getter also reads the current route and creates a DataManager when accountId changes; cache-key requests use that route account. This is explicit selection logic, not proof of all authorization or asynchronous switching behavior.

Existing request-spec source asserts unauthenticated rejection, bare-array list, search ranking/NUL removal, and successful CRUD. Cache-spec source exercises wrapper/bare-array doubles, cold/hit/changed-key behavior, account switching with equal cache keys, network bypass and IndexedDB failure. These are assertions present in source, not executed results; the bare-array double mirrors rather than imports the production subclass.
